questions.title: Present Simple Outpost
questions.instruction: Choose the correct form of the verb for he / she / it sentences.

parts.prompt: a. She ___ up at half past six every day.
parts.explanation: With he/she/it the verb takes -s: She gets up at half past six.

parts.prompt: b. He ___ his face in the morning.
parts.explanation: Verbs ending in -sh take -es with he/she/it: washes.

parts.prompt: c. My father ___ to work by car.
parts.explanation: “Go” takes -es with he/she/it: goes.

parts.prompt: d. Dan ___ his homework after lunch.
parts.explanation: “Do” becomes “does” with he/she/it: Dan does his homework.

questions.title: Intel File: Sami's Family
questions.instruction: Read the text. Then choose True or False for each sentence.
questions.passage: Hello! My name is Sami. I am ten years old. There are four people in my family: my father, my mother, my sister Hala and me — a small, happy family. My father is tall and thin, and he has got brown eyes. My mother has got short black hair and green eyes. My sister Hala is eight years old. She has got long blond hair and big blue eyes.

parts.explanation: True — the text says there are four people in the family.

parts.prompt: c. Hala has got blue eyes.

parts.prompt: b. How does Adam go to school?

parts.prompt: c. What does Adam do at four o'clock?
parts.explanation: At four o'clock Adam does his homework.

questions.title: Intel File: Huda's Flat
questions.instruction: Read the text about Huda's home. Then choose True or False for each sentence.
questions.passage: Hi! I'm Huda. I live in a flat with my family. There are four rooms in our flat: two bedrooms, a small kitchen and a big living room. In the living room, there is a long sofa and there are two armchairs. There is also a big TV on the wall. My bedroom is small, but it has got a bed, a desk and a wardrobe. There are many books on my desk because I love reading.

parts.prompt: a. There are four rooms in Huda's flat.
parts.explanation: True — the text says there are four rooms.

parts.prompt: b. There is one armchair in the living room.
parts.explanation: False — there are TWO armchairs in the living room.

parts.prompt: c. Huda's bedroom has got a wardrobe.
parts.explanation: True — her bedroom has got a bed, a desk and a wardrobe.

ref.activity: House/rooms reading (original passage) · bedroom text
ref.detail: Rooms, furniture, there is/are in a description text.

parts.prompt: Start like this: “My name's … . I'm from … .”
parts.correctAnswer: See the grading rubric criteria below.
parts.explanation: A full introduction has two short sentences: one with your name and one with your country — e.g. “My name's Hadi. I'm from Jordan.”

criteria.description: You tell your name (use “My name's …”, “My name is …”, “I'm …” or “I am …”).
You say where you are from (use the word “from”).
You write at least 6 words in total.

ref.activity: Ex. 3 (practise the conversation) · Ex. 9 (write about yourself frame)

questions.title: Have Got / Has Got Outpost
questions.instruction: Choose have got or has got to complete each sentence.

parts.explanation: With “I” we use “have got”: I have got two sisters.
“My grandfather” is one person (he), so we use “has got”.

parts.prompt: c. They ___ a new teacher this year.
parts.explanation: With “they” we use “have got”.
“Tina” is one person (she), so we use “has got”.

ref.activity: Act. 7b (choose has/have) · Let's Learn p. 8
ref.detail: have got → I/you/we/they; has got → he/she/it.

questions.title: Describe the Target
questions.instruction: Fill in each space with is or are.

parts.explanation: One person (he) takes “is”: He is tall and thin.
“Two sisters” is plural, so it takes “are”.
“Hair” takes “is” here: His hair is black.

ref.activity: Let's Learn p. 8: is + adjective describes the whole person
ref.detail: is with singular / hair; are with plural nouns when describing people.

questions.title: Build the Sentence
questions.instruction: Put the words in the correct order to make a sentence about the girl.

questions.title: Present Simple Outpost
questions.instruction: Choose the correct form of the verb for he / she / it sentences.

parts.prompt: a. She ___ up at half past six every day.
parts.explanation: With he/she/it the verb takes -s: She gets up at half past six.

parts.prompt: b. He ___ his face in the morning.
parts.explanation: Verbs ending in -sh take -es with he/she/it: washes.

parts.prompt: c. My father ___ to work by car.
parts.explanation: “Go” takes -es with he/she/it: goes.

parts.prompt: d. Dan ___ his homework after lunch.
parts.explanation: “Do” becomes “does” with he/she/it: Dan does his homework.

ref.activity: Acts. 4–5 (he/she gets up, makes the bed…) · WB p. 13

questions.title: There Is / There Are Stronghold
questions.instruction: Fill in each space with is, are, isn't or aren't.

parts.prompt: a. There ___ a small garden behind our house.
parts.explanation: “A garden” is singular: There is a small garden.

parts.prompt: b. There ___ two bathrooms in my house.
parts.explanation: “Two bathrooms” is plural: There are two bathrooms.

parts.prompt: c. There ___ any trees in our street.
parts.explanation: “Any” signals a negative plural sentence: There aren't any trees.

parts.prompt: d. Look! There ___ a sofa in the kitchen. It is in the wrong room!
parts.explanation: Singular and negative: There isn't a sofa in the kitchen.

questions.title: Intel File: Sami's Family
questions.instruction: Read the text. Then choose True or False for each sentence.
questions.passage: Hello! My name is Sami. I am ten years old. There are four people in my family: my father, my mother, my sister Hala and me — a small, happy family. My father is tall and thin, and he has got brown eyes. My mother has got short black hair and green eyes. My sister Hala is eight years old. She has got long blond hair and big blue eyes.

parts.prompt: a. Sami's family has got four people.
parts.explanation: True — the text says there are four people in the family.

parts.prompt: c. Hala has got blue eyes.

questions.title: Intel File: Adam's Day
questions.instruction: Read the text about Adam's daily routine. Then answer the questions.
questions.passage: Meet Adam. Adam is ten years old and he is in grade four. Every morning, Adam gets up at seven o'clock. He washes his face and brushes his teeth. Then he has breakfast with his family at quarter past seven. Adam goes to school by car, and school finishes at two o'clock. At home, Adam does his homework at four o'clock. In the evening, he has dinner with his family and sometimes watches TV. At nine o'clock, he goes to bed.

parts.prompt: a. What time does Adam get up?
parts.explanation: The text says: “Adam gets up at seven o'clock.”

parts.prompt: b. How does Adam go to school?
parts.explanation: The text says Adam goes to school by car. The bus and walking are not mentioned.

parts.prompt: c. What does Adam do at four o'clock?
parts.explanation: At four o'clock Adam does his homework.

ref.detail: Routine activities + telling the time in a continuous text.

questions.title: Intel File: Huda's Flat

In the living room, there is a long sofa and there are two armchairs. There is also a big TV on the wall. My bedroom is small, but it has got a bed, a desk and a wardrobe. There are many books on my desk because I love reading.

parts.prompt: b. There is one armchair in the living room.
parts.explanation: False — there are TWO armchairs in the living room.

questions.title: Present Simple Outpost
questions.instruction: Choose the correct form of the verb for he / she / it sentences.

parts.explanation: Verbs ending in -sh take -es with he/she/it: washes.

parts.prompt: c. My father ___ to work by car.
parts.explanation: “Go” takes -es with he/she/it: goes.

parts.explanation: “Do” becomes “does” with he/she/it: Dan does his homework.
